# Later capability tests: specifications only

**None of these tests was run.** No test scene, render, export or `.blend` was generated by this research. Expected observations below are hypotheses derived from documentation/source. Each future attempt needs the pinned build identity, source/parameters, unique output root, logs, exit status and retained failure artifacts. Do not erase failures or replace them with a successful retry.

## T01. Execution and exception status

Run a minimal normal-return script, an unhandled `RuntimeError`, a caught exception, and `SystemExit(0)` / `SystemExit(3)` as separate processes with the same documented command prefix. Set `--python-exit-code 17` before the script; compare a deliberately late flag in an isolated diagnostic case.

Expected: normal completion is distinct from unhandled script failure; caught failure can appear successful unless the script fails deliberately; SystemExit follows its own exit path. Record actual codes and stdout/stderr. Failure criterion: the host accepts an unhandled failure, the baseline drifts, or documented/source expectations differ without explanation. A native crash is a separate outcome, not “Python raised.”

## T02. Exception after partial scene mutation

Create one owned ID, deliberately raise before saving, and inspect within a controlled catch in that same process. Separately allow the exception to escape. A third case writes a partial file before raising.

Expected: in-memory changes made before the exception remain in the caught case; a fresh process does not inherit them; an earlier disk file can remain after process failure. Failure criterion: recovery assumes rollback or publishes an incomplete attempt. Retain the partial file and error record. Do not mutate an accepted scene for this test.

## T03. Repeated execution and sharing

Call the chosen revision routine twice in a disposable scene with one owned part. Add an intentional duplicate ownership key in a separate case. Compare Object and Mesh counts, keys and data-sharing relationships. Also compare `Object.copy()` with copy-plus-`data.copy()` after a vertex edit.

Expected: controlled rerun yields one semantic part, intentional shared copies share geometry, independent copies don't; ambiguous keys cause a clear failure. Failure criterion: `.001` accumulation, unrelated data deletion, silently choosing the first duplicate, or unintended shared mutation.

## T04. Context-dependent operator failure

Use a deliberate wrong-mode/wrong-active-object case for modifier application, then the documented Object Mode/local single-user setup in a separate owned scene. Include a viewport-dependent operation only as a negative headless test, not as a production requirement.

Expected: polling/errors distinguish unsuitable context; direct data construction still works without UI selection. Failure criterion: pretending a fabricated area solves UI requirements, status-only acceptance despite an unchanged stack, or partial mutation unrecorded.

## T05. Original versus evaluated geometry

Construct a mesh with a topology-changing modifier and compare original counts, refreshed evaluated counts and render/viewport settings. Repeat with the bounded instance graph before and after Realize Instances. Inspect copied world-space coordinates and temporary-mesh cleanup; do not intentionally dereference freed native memory.

Expected: original data remains authored, evaluated output reflects enabled settings, instance-only output differs from a realized mesh, and temporary results are not attached as original IDs. Failure criterion: stale graph data, missing instance placements, mismatched evaluation mode or reuse after cleanup. Include delayed subdivision materialization and preserve-all-data-layer behavior explicitly.

## T06. Save/reopen and resources

Save a scene containing owned parameters, a curve, modifiers, a node group/input, shared data and neutral inspection settings. Reopen in a new process, reacquire all IDs and compare semantic structure/evaluated summaries. In a separate disposable case, introduce a small task-owned external resource, then make it unavailable; do not download a finished model.

Expected: retained original data/settings survive; process locals don't; missing resources are detected and preserved in the failure record. Failure criterion: missing IDs/input values, hidden reliance on a source script or external resource, incorrect relative root, or accepting a file solely by size.

## T07. Invalid topology, normals and modifier order

Supply deliberately invalid indices/duplicate face vertices to a disposable constructor, record `validate` repairs, and reject unintended repair. Use valid comparison shapes for Bevel→Solidify versus Solidify→Bevel and custom/smooth versus flat normals. Include a zero-size dimension axis and nonuniform Object scale.

Expected: storage validation is distinguishable from geometric/manifold quality; order and scale affect measured geometry; shading can change appearance without topology change. Failure criterion: “validate returned True” interpreted as untouched valid input, geometric claims based only on smooth rendering, or asserted wall thickness without measurement.

## T08. Render/export failure and stale output

Render an ordinary still, then separate cases with missing camera and unwritable/invalid destination. Attempt OBJ export of an empty filtered collection. Seed an old file only in an explicitly identified negative-test directory; the production host must use fresh directories.

Expected: log/status/file observations remain separate; empty OBJ export may finish with warning and no file; old files never satisfy a new job. Validate PNG signature, dimensions and readability with an image reader, then inspect the image. Failure criterion: exit/status-only acceptance, missing expected artifact, silently reused PNG or unbounded process hang. Record wall-clock timeout separately from Cycles time limits.

## T09. Static export information loss

Export evaluated owned geometry with explicit axes/scale/materials. Read OBJ/MTL as text and reopen in the chosen receiver if later authorized. Compare positions, face/normal/UV/material assignments and expected losses against `.blend`. Compare `apply_transform=True/False` in separate cases.

Expected: static geometry/limited materials transfer, procedural stacks/groups/parents/units do not; generated texture graphs are not automatically baked. Failure criterion: assuming editable procedural equivalence, wrong axis/unit interpretation, missing instance geometry, or claiming lossless materials from a nonempty MTL.

## T10. Blender 5.2 migration

Compare typed `.properties.inputs.<identifier>.value` assignment with a deliberate historical `modifier['Socket_...']` assignment. Preserve returned interface identifiers, recreate a socket with the same display name in a separate case, and record the resulting schema. Check Transform Geometry's Mode socket and deprecated `use_nodes` behavior. Do not open in older Blender as part of this fixed-baseline test.

Expected: typed input affects the consumed value; same name need not preserve identity; legacy metadata assignment may be inert; unsupported old API paths fail or are deprecated. Failure criterion: incorrect migration mapping, silently skipped parameters or a documentation/source mismatch treated as runtime success.

## Decision after tests

A result is accepted only against the test-specific observations, not because the code is plausible, syntax parses, a process returns zero or one image looks good. Preserve all success, failure, partial and inconclusive receipts. If the build changes, establish a new baseline before comparing outcomes.
